Responde (By Shri Mohd. Nasir - Advocate for the respondent no.1 and Shri Sourabh Makhija - Advocate for the respondent no.2)
This appeal coming on for 01.05.2024 this day, the court passed the following:

ORDER The present appeal has been filed by the injured-claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.2000/- granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal") vide award dated 16.02.2004 in MAC Case No.2/2004 filed under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The learned Tribunal on the appraisal of facts, pleading and evidence on record heard that the claimant has been injured in motor vehicular accident that took place on 09.12.2001 due to rash and negligent driving of Zipsy bearing no.MO-K-8080 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending Lallo @ Suneel Dahiya vs Mohd. Akram on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173432253/
1 vehicle") was being driven by respondent no.1, owned by second respondent.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal awarded compensation amount of Rs.2000/-.
The liability to pay compensation on the second respondent.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation on the ground that learned Tribunal has failed to consider the disability certificate issued by the Doctor dated 13.07.2002 and further stated that the learned Tribunal failed to consider the medical expenses which were spent by the claimant in treatment and also not awarded any amount for pain and suffering.

Further submit that the amount of compensation may be determined in view of fracture sustained by the claimant and the amount spent towards medical treatment which may be just and reasonable to enhance the compensation and further submit that the amount awarded is very meager and deserves to be enhanced.
5. On perusal of impugned award would show that the learned Tribunal has framed issue no.1 "as to whether the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by its driver" to which the Tribunal after considering the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 coupled with the documentary evidence has categorically observed in para-11 of the impugned award that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle Zipsy bearing no.MO-K-8080 by its driver (the first respondent), therefore, there is no reason to interfere with the findings of learned Tribunal that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing No.MO K 8080.
6.
Perused the record shows that at the time of the accident, the injured was 15 years age.

Upon consideration of the medical record the testimony of PW-1 injured and PW-2 eye witness to the incident and Doctors were not examined to speak about the nature of injuries sustained by him and the disability certificate Ex.P-7 issued by Doctor Anand Shrivastava, Jabalpur but he was not examined and PW-1 has not stated that he was treated by Doctor Anand Shrivastava and the disability certificate has not been issued by Medical Board

, therefore, much weight cannot be given to disability certificate Ex.P-7, as there is no basis to believe that the appellant/claimant suffering with disability and the Ex.P-2 wound certificate issued by Doctor reflects minor injuries.
The learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards medical expenses and PW-1 has not produced any medical bills showing the expenses of 15,000/-.
The appellant who was a minor and his mother is illiterate and they are not supposed to be that much of meticulous to maintain the bills for future use.
He must have incurred some amount towards medical expenses, therefore, the claimant has been awarded Rs.5000/- towards medical expenses due to injury sustained in the right toe.
The compensation under the head of medical expenses of Rs.5,000/- is sufficient.

7. In the instant case, the Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards pain and suffering certainly by the time of accident the claimant is aged about 15 years and he sustained injuries on the right toe definitely he might have suffered with pain, therefore, it needs to award of Rs.5,000/- for pain and sufferance.
The sufferance of injured cannot be compensated in terms of money

, therefore,
compensation under the head of pain and suffering is awarded Rs.5,000/-.

sentences.text:
In Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1 the Hon'ble Apex Court, while elaborating the concept of 'just compensation' observed as under:
"Just compensation is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit."

9. On an overall re-appreciation of the pleadings, material on record and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the afore-cited decision, I am of the definite opinion that the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhancement of compensation as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below for easy reference."
 S. Name of the Head Amount Enhanced/
 No awarded by Reduced by this  the learned Court in Rs.
 Tribunal  1 Medical Expenses and pain and suffering 2000/- 10,000/-
 Total 2,000/- 10,000/-
 (-) Compensation awarded By the Tribunal 2000/-

Enhanced amount 8,000/-
10.
The Tribunals are expected to make an award by determining the amount of compensation which should appear to be just and proper.

In the present case, the compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal, against 1. 2009 ACJ 1298 (SC) the background of the facts and circumstances of the case, is not just and reasonable and the claimant is entitled to more compensation.

11. Therefore, in view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the opinion that the award passed by the Tribunal warrants interference and thereby enhanced the compensation from Rs.2,000/- to Rs.10,000/-.

12. Resultantly, the appeal is allowed and the compensation amount is enhanced from Rs.2000/- to Rs.10,000/- along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, against the Respondent no.2.

(ii) Respondent no.2/Commissioner, Municipal Corporation, Katni is directed to deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this judgment, failing which, execution can be taken out against respondent no.2.
